issues.legal_issue: Amounts due for a statutory liquor-selling privilege may be recovered under the statutory revenue-recovery mechanism even when no formally executed government contract exists.
material_facts: The appellants successfully bid for toddy shops and paid the required initial amounts on demand.
The auction conditions required payment of the balance and execution of agreements before licences were issued.
The appellants were allowed to begin operating the shops but did not pay the remaining amounts.
No agreement complying with the constitutional requirements for government contracts was executed.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a formally executed contract did not prevent recovery of the amounts due under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Kerala Abkari Act permits recovery of amounts due from a grantee of a privilege and does not make a formally executed contract a condition precedent to recovery. Statutory liabilities may be enforced under statutory provisions, and equitable obligations may also be enforced independently of the formal-contract requirements of Article 299 of the Constitution. The Court approved Madhavan v. Assistant Excise Commissioner, Palghat, and referred to Union of India v. A. L. Ralia Ram, Mulamchand v. State of Madhya Pradesh, and the restitution principle stated in Nelson v. Harbolt.

rule.if: liquor_privilege_recovery_case and successful_auction_bid and formal_contract_not_executed and unpaid_balance

predicates.liquor_privilege_recovery_case: The proceeding seeks recovery of unpaid amounts relating to a statutory privilege to sell liquor.
predicates.successful_auction_bid: A bidder succeeded at an auction for the privilege and accepted the auction conditions.
predicates.formal_contract_not_executed: The parties did not execute a formal written contract for the privilege.
predicates.unpaid_balance: The successful bidder did not pay the balance required under the auction conditions.

issues.definition: When a liquor-privilege recovery proceeding concerns a successful bidder who has left the required balance unpaid, the absence of a formal contract does not prevent recovery through revenue proceedings.

issues.legal_issue: A successful bidder permitted to exercise a liquor-selling privilege before receiving a licence may be treated as a grantee for statutory recovery purposes.
material_facts: The appellants succeeded in auctions for toddy-shop privileges and paid the amounts demanded initially.
The excise authorities allowed the appellants to sell liquor before licences were issued and before agreements were executed.
The appellants did not pay the remaining amounts due.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were grantees for the purposes of statutory recovery despite not having received licences or executed written agreements.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18A(1) and 18A(2) of the Kerala Abkari Act contemplate that a person may be a grantee before receiving a licence, although the privilege cannot be exercised until a licence is received. Section 28 uses “grantee” broadly enough to cover persons whom excise authorities permit to exercise the privilege in recognition and anticipation of their rights to receive licences. The Court approved Madhavan v. Assistant Excise Commissioner, Palghat.

predicates.liquor_privilege_recovery_case: The proceeding seeks recovery of unpaid amounts relating to a statutory privilege to sell liquor.
predicates.successful_auction_bid: A bidder succeeded at an auction for the privilege and accepted the auction conditions.
predicates.authorities_permitted_exercise_before_li: The relevant authorities allowed the successful bidder to exercise the privilege before issuing a licence.

issues.definition: A successful bidder permitted by the authorities to exercise a liquor-selling privilege before receiving a licence is treated as a grantee for recovery purposes.

issues.legal_issue: A bidder's payment obligations become enforceable when the government permits the bidder to operate under the privilege, even though the contemplated agreements and licences have not yet been completed.
material_facts: The auction conditions required the appellants to pay the remaining amounts due.
The appellants had paid the demanded initial amounts.
The government allowed the appellants to begin selling liquor before the agreements were executed and licences issued.
The appellants did not pay the remaining amounts.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were bound to perform their corresponding payment obligations, and those obligations had operative force through statutory sanction and equity.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the government had performed its part by allowing the appellants to begin selling liquor, while the appellants remained bound by the corresponding obligations imposed under auction conditions issued pursuant to statutory authority. The reciprocal obligations had operative force through statutory sanction and equity, apart from any contractual basis.

rule.if: liquor_privilege_auction_case and auction_terms_required_balance_payment and government_permitted_business and bidder_left_balance_unpaid

predicates.liquor_privilege_auction_case: The proceeding concerns an auction for a statutory privilege to sell liquor.
predicates.auction_terms_required_balance_payment: The auction conditions required the successful bidder to pay a remaining balance.
predicates.government_permitted_business: The government allowed the successful bidder to begin operating under the privilege.
predicates.bidder_left_balance_unpaid: The successful bidder did not pay the required remaining balance.

issues.definition: When auction conditions require a balance payment and the government permits the bidder to operate, a bidder who leaves that balance unpaid remains bound to pay it.
